name: Timer & Calculator
description: A timer and stopwatch calculator for time-based measurements, countdown, and chronometer functions.
guide: Tap to count beats or breaths over a set duration (default 15 seconds). Calculates rate per minute from taps and elapsed time. Useful for heart rate and respiratory rate measurement.

name: Basic Calculator
description: A simple calculator for basic arithmetic operations including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
guide: Basic arithmetic calculator supporting addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, percentages, and square roots. Use for general math calculations.

name: Laboratory Unit Converter
description: Convert between SI and conventional units for laboratory values including glucose, creatinine, urea, and other blood tests.
guide: Convert between SI and conventional units for laboratory values including sodium, potassium, creatinine, urea, and other blood tests using hydrated molecular weights and valence.

name: Glucose Unit Converter
description: Convert blood glucose values between mg/dL and mmol/L units.
guide: Convert blood glucose between mg/dL and mmol/L with fasting/random category interpretation: hypoglycemia (<70), normal (70-100 fasting), prediabetes (100-125), diabetes (≥126).

name: Drug Dosage Calculator
description: Calculate drug dosage based on patient weight and prescribed dose per kg.
guide: Calculate drug dosage based on patient weight and prescribed dose per kg. Supports per-kg, per-kg-per-day, per-minute, and per-kg-per-minute infusion rates with duration input.

name: Drug Volume Calculator
description: Calculate the volume of medication to administer based on concentration and required dose.
guide: Calculate the volume of medication to administer using the formula: Volume (mL) = Dose × (Supply Volume ÷ Supply Amount).

name: Drug Unit Converter
description: Convert electrolyte units between mmol/L, mg/dL, and other common measurements for potassium, sodium, chloride, and more.
guide: Convert electrolyte units between mmol/L, mg/dL, grams, and mEq for potassium, sodium, chloride, magnesium, and calcium salts using hydrated molecular weights and valence.

name: IV Fluid Drop Rate
description: Calculate IV infusion rate and drip rate for fluid therapy administration.
guide: Calculate IV infusion rate and drip rate in drops per minute using drop factors: IV set 20 gtt/mL, blood set 15 gtt/mL, soluset 60 gtt/mL. Formula: drops/min = Volume × drop factor ÷ time in minutes.

name: BMI Calculator
description: Calculate Body Mass Index (BMI) from weight and height, with WHO classification categories.
guide: BMI = Weight (kg) ÷ [Height (m)]². WHO Classification: <18.5 Underweight, 18.5–24.9 Normal weight, 25–29.9 Overweight, 30–34.9 Obese Class I, 35–39.9 Obese Class II, ≥40 Obese Class III (Morbid).

name: qSOFA & mSOFA
description: Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score for sepsis and organ dysfunction evaluation.
guide: qSOFA: RR ≥22, SBP ≤100, GCS <15 (score 0-3). mSOFA: respiratory (SpO2/FiO2), liver (jaundice), cardiovascular (MAP/vasopressor), CNS (GCS), renal (creatinine) subscores. Interpretation: No organ dysfunction, Mild, Moderate, or Severe dysfunction.

name: SpO₂ / FiO₂ Ratio
description: Calculate the oxygenation index (SpO2/FiO2 ratio) for assessing respiratory function.
guide: S/F Ratio = SpO₂ (%) ÷ FiO₂. ARDS oxygenation severity: >315 does not meet threshold, 235–315 mild, 148–235 moderate, ≤148 severe. SpO₂ reference: 95–100% normal, 90–94% mild hypoxemia, below 90% significant, below 85% severe.

name: Glasgow Coma Scale
description: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) for assessing level of consciousness in patients with brain injury.
guide: Glasgow Coma Scale: Eye response (1-4), Verbal response (1-5), Motor response (1-6). Total score 3-15. Interpretation: ≤8 Severe head injury, 9-12 Moderate, 13-15 Mild.

name: Shock Index
description: Calculate Shock Index (heart rate divided by systolic blood pressure) to assess hemodynamic stability.
guide: Shock Index = Heart Rate ÷ Systolic BP. Interpretation: <0.5 Low, 0.5–0.7 Normal, 0.8–0.9 Borderline (monitor closely), ≥1.0 High risk of haemorrhagic shock / need urgent intervention.

name: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP)
description: Calculate Mean Arterial Pressure from systolic and diastolic blood pressure values.
guide: MAP = DBP + ⅓(SBP − DBP). Pulse Pressure = SBP − DBP. Reference ranges: <65 Low (organ hypoperfusion risk), 65–100 Normal, >100 Elevated (hypertension). Normal pulse pressure ~40 mmHg.

name: Rule of Nines
description: Estimate total body surface area (TBSA) burned using the Rule of Nines for adult and pediatric patients.
guide: Wallace Rule of Nines adult TBSA breakdown: Head & Neck 9% (4.5% anterior, 4.5% posterior), Each Arm 9% (4.5% ant, 4.5% post), Anterior Trunk 18% (chest 9%, abdomen 9%), Posterior Trunk 18% (upper back 9%, lower back 9%), Each Leg 18% (9% ant, 9% post), Perineum 1%.

name: Parkland Formula
description: Calculate fluid resuscitation requirements for burn patients using the Parkland formula.
guide: Total Fluid (24h) = 4 mL × Weight (kg) × %TBSA. Give 50% in the first 8 hours (from time of burn), remaining 50% over the next 16 hours. Fluid of choice: Ringer's Lactate. Maximum TBSA capped at 50% to prevent fluid overload.

name: Fluid Correction
description: Calculate maintenance fluid therapy and fluid correction requirements.
guide: Fluid Deficit = % dehydration × Weight (kg) × 10. Maintenance (Holliday–Segar): 100 mL/kg for first 10 kg + 50 mL/kg for next 10 kg + 20 mL/kg for remainder. Dehydration severity: mild 5%, moderate 10%, severe 15%.

name: eGFR Calculator
description: Estimate Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) for assessing kidney function.
guide: CKD-EPI 2021 Equation: eGFR = 142 × min(SCr/κ, 1)^α × max(SCr/κ, 1)^-1.200 × 0.9938^Age × (1.012 if female), where κ = 0.7 (female) / 0.9 (male), α = -0.241 (female) / -0.302 (male). KDIGO stages: G1 ≥90 normal, G2 60-89 mild, G3a 45-59, G3b 30-44, G4 15-29 severe, G5 <15 kidney failure.

name: Urea-Creatinine Ratio (UCR)
description: Calculate the urea-to-creatinine ratio for evaluating kidney function and prerenal azotemia.
guide: BUN/Cr Ratio (BUN mg/dL : Cr mg/dL): >20:1 Prerenal (e.g., severe dehydration), 10–20:1 Normal or Postrenal, <10:1 Intrarenal (e.g., acute tubular necrosis). Urea/Cr Ratio (mmol/L : mmol/L): >100:1 Prerenal, 40–100:1 Normal/Postrenal, <40:1 Intrarenal.

name: Anion Gap & Delta Ratio
description: Calculate anion gap and delta ratio for evaluating acid-base disorders and metabolic acidosis.
guide: Calculate anion gap and delta ratio for evaluating acid-base disorders and metabolic acidosis. Anion gap = Na − (Cl + HCO3). Delta ratio = delta gap / delta HCO3 to distinguish high vs normal anion gap acidosis and mixed disorders.

name: Serum Osmolality Calculator
description: Calculate serum osmolality from sodium, glucose, and BUN values.
guide: Calculated Osmolality = 2×Na⁺ + Glucose (mmol/L) + Urea (mmol/L). Osmol Gap = Measured Osmolality − Calculated Osmolality. Reference: Normal 275–295 mOsm/kg, normal osmol gap <10 mOsm/kg. Elevated gap suggests toxic alcohols, mannitol, or ketoacidosis.

name: Hypokalemia Correction
description: Calculate potassium replacement for hypokalemia correction.
guide: Potassium Deficit = (Target − Observed K⁺) × Weight (kg) × Constant (default 0.4). Maintenance = Weight (kg) × Rate (default 1 mmol/kg/day). Safety rules: ensure urine output ≥0.5 mL/kg/hr before IV replacement; max daily dose 120 mmol/day; max infusion rate 10–20 mmol/hr; max concentration 40 mmol/L (peripheral line).

name: Hyponatremia Correction
description: Calculate sodium correction for hyponatremia management.
guide: Adrogue–Madias formula for sodium correction: change in Na per liter = (Infusate Na − Patient Na) ÷ (TBW + 1). TBW factor: male nonelderly 0.6, male elderly 0.5, female nonelderly 0.5, female elderly 0.45. Aim for ≤8 mmol/L rise in 24 hours to avoid osmotic demyelination.

name: Corrected Sodium
description: Calculate corrected sodium values for patients with hyperglycemia.
guide: Corrected Sodium = Measured Na + 1.6 × ((Glucose mg/dL − 100) ÷ 100). Use for patients with hyperglycemia to obtain the true serum sodium concentration.

name: Corrected Calcium
description: Calculate corrected calcium values based on serum albumin levels.
guide: Payne Formula: Corrected Ca (mg/dL) = Measured Ca + 0.8 × (4 − Albumin g/dL); Corrected Ca (mmol/L) = Measured Ca + 0.02 × (40 − Albumin g/L). Reference range: Normal 8.5–10.5 mg/dL (2.12–2.62 mmol/L). <8.5 hypocalcemia, >10.5 hypercalcemia.

name: Calcium Phosphate Product
description: Calculate the calcium-phosphate product for assessing mineral metabolism disorders.
guide: Calcium-Phosphate Product = Calcium (mg/dL) × Phosphate (mg/dL). Risk cut-offs: <55 Low risk, 55–70 Moderate risk, >70 High risk of vascular calcification. Corrected calcium can be applied using albumin adjustment.

name: Blood Volume Calculator
description: Estimate total blood volume based on patient weight and height.
guide: Estimated Blood Volume = Weight (kg) × Age Constant (mL/kg). Age-based constants: Neonate 85–90, Infant 75–80, Child 70–75, Adult Male ~70, Adult Female ~65 mL/kg.

name: Pediatric Weight Estimator
description: Estimate weight for pediatric patients based on age.
guide: Pediatric weight estimation formulas based on age. Default (neonate ≤3 months): (age in days − 10) × 30 + birth weight ÷ 1000. Nelson: (months + 9) ÷ 2 (3-11 months), 2×years + 8 (1-6 years), 7×years − 5 (7-12 years). Best Guess: (months + 9) ÷ 2 (<12 months), 2×years + 5 (1-5 years), 4×years (5-14 years).

name: Pediatric Age Estimator
description: Estimate age for pediatric patients based on weight and height.
guide: Estimate age for pediatric patients based on weight and height using growth reference data.

name: APGAR Score
description: APGAR score for assessing newborn health immediately after birth.
guide: APGAR score assessed at 1, 5, and 10 minutes after birth. Five criteria: Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration (each scored 0-2). Total 0-10. Interpretation: ≥8 Excellent, 4-7 Fair, ≤3 Depressed.

name: Body Surface Area (BSA)
description: Calculate Body Surface Area (BSA) using various formulas for medication dosing.
guide: Mosteller Formula: BSA (m²) = √[Weight (kg) × Height (cm) ÷ 3600]. Average reference values: Adult male ~1.9 m², Adult female ~1.6 m², Children 9-12 years ~1.07 m², Infants ~0.25 m².

name: IV Fluid + Dextrose Calculator
description: Calculate dextrose concentration and volume for IV fluid fortification in pediatric patients.
guide: Withdraw and Replace Method (constant volume): Volume to replace = [Bag Volume × (Target % − Current %)] ÷ (Stock % − Current %). Withdraw the calculated volume from the bag, then add the same volume of stock dextrose (e.g., D50).

name: Ballard Score Calculator
description: Ballard Score for assessing gestational age of newborns.
guide: New Ballard Score assesses neuromuscular and physical maturity to estimate gestational age in newborns. Score -10 to 50 maps to 20-44 weeks. Formula: Gestational Age (weeks) = 20 + [0.4 × (Total Score + 10)], rounded down.

name: Pregnancy Calculator
description: Calculate estimated gestational age (EGA) and estimated due date (EDD) from LMP or ultrasound.
guide: Calculate estimated gestational age (EGA) and estimated due date (EDD) from last menstrual period (LMP). EDD = LMP + 280 days. Trimester: <13 weeks First, 13–27 weeks Second, ≥28 weeks Third.

name: Bishop Score
description: Bishop Score for assessing cervical readiness for labor induction.
guide: Traditional Bishop Score: cervical dilation, effacement, station, position, consistency (total 0-13). Modified Bishop Score: dilation, cervical length, station. Interpretation: >8 (traditional) or ≥5 (modified) = favorable cervix, high likelihood of successful induction; ≤8 / <5 = unfavorable.

name: Wells Score DVT
description: Wells Score for assessing probability of deep vein thrombosis (DVT).
guide: Wells DVT criteria (each +1 unless noted): active cancer, paralysis/immobilization, bedridden ≥3 days or surgery ≤12 weeks, localized tenderness, entire leg swollen, calf swelling ≥3cm, pitting edema, collateral superficial veins, previous DVT, alternative diagnosis more likely (-2). Score ≥2 = DVT likely (Doppler USS); ≤1 = DVT unlikely (D-Dimer). 3-tier: ≥3 high (53%), 1-2 moderate (17%), ≤0 low (5%).

name: Wells Score PE
description: Wells Score for assessing probability of pulmonary embolism (PE).
guide: Wells PE criteria: clinical signs of DVT (3), PE most likely diagnosis (3), HR >100 (1.5), immobilization ≥3 days or surgery ≤4 weeks (1.5), previous DVT/PE (1.5), hemoptysis (1), malignancy (1). Score >6 = high risk (CTPA); ≤6 = unlikely (D-Dimer). 3-tier: >6 high (~65%), 2-6 moderate (~30%), <2 low (~10%).

name: Siriraj Stroke Score
description: Siriraj Stroke Score for differentiating hemorrhagic from ischemic stroke.
guide: Siriraj Stroke Score (SSS) = (2.5 × Consciousness) + (2 × Vomiting) + (2 × Headache) + (0.1 × Diastolic BP) − (3 × Atheroma) − 12. Interpretation: >1 likely hemorrhagic stroke, <−1 likely ischemic stroke, −1 to 1 indeterminate (imaging required). Atheroma: DM, claudication, angina/ACS, or history of TIA.

name: CHA2DS2-VASc Score
description: CHA2DS2-VASc score for assessing stroke risk in atrial fibrillation patients.
guide: CHA2DS2-VASc score for stroke risk in atrial fibrillation: Congestive heart failure (1), Hypertension (1), Age ≥75 (2), Diabetes (1), Stroke/TIA/thromboembolism (2), Vascular disease (1), Age 65-74 (1), Sex category female (1). Maximum score 9. Higher score = higher annual stroke risk, anticoagulation considered.

name: CURB-65 Score
description: CURB-65 score for assessing severity of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).
guide: CURB-65 criteria (1 point each): Confusion, Urea >7 mmol/L, Respiratory rate ≥30/min, Blood pressure (SBP <90 or DBP ≤60), Age ≥65 years. Score 0-5. Higher score = higher 30-day mortality risk; guides inpatient vs outpatient management.

name: Framingham HF Criteria
description: Framingham criteria for diagnosing heart failure.
guide: Framingham criteria for heart failure: Diagnosis requires ≥2 Major criteria OR 1 Major + ≥2 Minor criteria. Major: paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, jugular venous distension, pulmonary rales, cardiomegaly, acute pulmonary edema, S3 gallop, CVP >16 cmH2O, circulation time ≥25 sec, weight loss ≥4.5 kg on therapy. Minor: ankle edema, nocturnal cough, dyspnea on exertion, hepatomegaly, pleural effusion, heart rate ≥120 bpm.

name: DAR Risk Assessment (2026)
description: DAR Risk Assessment for diabetes risk during Ramadan fasting.
guide: DAR Risk Assessment scores diabetes-related risk during Ramadan fasting across 14 domains: pregnancy, diabetes type, duration, treatment, hypoglycemia, HbA1c, monitoring, emergencies, macrovascular disease, eGFR, microvascular complications, frailty, physical labor, education, fasting hours. Score ≤3 Low risk, ≤6 Moderate risk, >6 High risk (do not fast).

name: ECG Axis Calculator
description: Calculate cardiac axis from ECG leads to determine normal, left, or right axis deviation.
guide: 3-lead method estimates cardiac axis from net QRS deflection in Lead I and Lead aVF. I positive + aVF positive = Normal axis (−30° to +90°); I positive + aVF negative = Left axis deviation (<−30°); I negative + aVF positive = Right axis deviation (>+90°); I negative + aVF negative = Extreme axis (beyond ±150°). Hexaxial dial reference included.

name: ECG Waveform Guide
description: ECG waveform reference guide with intervals, segments, and cardiac rhythm interpretation.
guide: ECG wave measurement guide: P wave (start to end of P), PR interval (start of P to start of QRS), QRS complex (start of Q to end of S), QT interval (start of Q to end of T), ST segment (end of S/J point to start of T), T wave (start to end of T), heart rate (one R wave to next R). Voltage references: P wave <2.5 mm limb / <1.5 mm chest; QRS ≥5 mm limb / ≥10 mm chest. ST elevation/depression criteria included.

name: IPSS
description: International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) for assessing benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) symptoms.
guide: IPSS assesses lower urinary tract symptoms: incomplete emptying, frequency, intermittency, urgency, weak stream, straining, nocturia (each scored 0-5). Total 0-35. Interpretation: ≤7 Mild, 8-19 Moderate, 20-35 Severe. Quality of life question also included.

name: Mini-Mental State Exam
description: Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) for assessing cognitive impairment and dementia.
guide: MMSE assesses cognitive function across 11 domains: orientation (10), registration (3), attention (5), recall (3), naming (2), repetition (1), 3-stage command (3), reading (1), writing (1), copying (1). Total 0-30. Interpretation: 24-30 Normal, 18-23 Mild impairment, 0-17 Severe impairment.

name: SAAG Calculator
description: Serum Ascites Albumin Gradient (SAAG) for evaluating the cause of ascites.
guide: SAAG = Serum Albumin − Ascitic Fluid Albumin. High SAAG (≥1.1 g/dL) indicates portal hypertension: cirrhosis, alcoholic hepatitis, cardiac failure, Budd-Chiari syndrome. Low SAAG (<1.1 g/dL) indicates non-portal cause: peritoneal carcinomatosis, TB peritonitis, pancreatitis, nephrotic syndrome.

name: Dialysis Adequacy
description: Calculate dialysis adequacy using URR (urea reduction ratio) and Kt/V for hemodialysis patients.
guide: URR (Urea Reduction Ratio) = [(Pre BUN − Post BUN) ÷ Pre BUN] × 100. Units cancel — valid regardless of mmol/L or mg/dL. Adequacy targets: URR ≥65% = adequate HD session (KDOQI target); URR <65% = inadequate — review session time, blood flow rate, or access. Kt/V ≥1.2 equivalent adequacy measure.
